query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Integrating a machine‐learned interatomic potential (MLIP) trained on ab initio liquid snapshots of a multicomponent HEA into the thermodynamic‐integration reference ensemble will substantially improve reference–target phase‐space overlap and reduce the thermodynamic‐integration path mismatch relative to TOR‐TILD’s standard EAM references.
generation.material_initial_state: Liquid equimolar Ni–Co–Fe–Cr–Mn high‐entropy alloy at and near its melting temperature (Tm to Tm+200 K).
generation.intervention: Replace the EAM reference potential in the TOR‐TILD thermodynamic integration scheme with an MLIP trained on ab initio molecular dynamics snapshots of the HEA liquid.
generation.conditions: Ambient pressure; temperature range Tm ≤ T ≤ Tm + 200 K; equimolar five‐component HEA.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced accuracy of local coordination environments and force distributions in the MLIP relative to EAM.
generation.mechanism: By more faithfully reproducing ab initio forces and liquid structure, the MLIP reference ensemble samples configurations more representative of the target ab initio liquid, increasing overlap and lowering integration barriers.
generation.predicted_outcome: Reduction of the thermodynamic‐integration path mismatch by approximately 30–50% compared with TOR‐TILD using standard EAM references.
generation.baseline: Path mismatch metric obtained by TOR‐TILD with standard EAM references for the same HEA liquid.
generation.boundary: Applicable to multicomponent HEA liquids near melting; not validated for solid phases or single‐component liquids.
generation.uncertainty: ±20% on the estimated reduction in mismatch; performance untested for >5 components or non‐equimolar ratios.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform thermodynamic integration of the equimolar NiCoFeCrMn liquid free energy at Tm and Tm+100 K using (a) TOR‐TILD with standard EAM reference and (b) TOR‐TILD with the MLIP reference. Independently compute the ab initio free energy via direct adiabatic switching. Quantify the integration path mismatch in each case.
measurements: Path mismatch metric (e.g. average squared force difference along the integration path)
Absolute free‐energy difference to direct ab initio benchmark
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the MLIP‐based reference does not achieve at least a 20% reduction in path mismatch relative to the EAM reference at both temperatures, the hypothesis is falsified.
